solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: the dam word stands before the time word in the answer

parts.note: a dam checks or holds back water
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone consults the clock before checking what a purchase cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the bill is the damage, as in asking what the damage is when wanting the price.

clue.text: South of Land's End, is island separate?

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means the pieces sit below that letter
the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Is there an island off the coast below Land's End, standing apart?
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the far tip of Cornwall, but here it is the last letter of 'Land'.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct and individually separate things are discrete, like discrete units.

clue.text: Replacement of alarm essential — it's absolute rubbish

indicators.note: replacement of means the letters are put back in a different order

parts.note: key means essential or vital

explanation.surface: Swapping out an essential alarm is said to be nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal word for nonsense or humbug talk.

clue.text: Burn in green initially, then blue

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: blue means sad or low in spirits

explanation.surface: A flame burns green at first and then blue.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn gently with light and no flame is to give off a steady glow.

clue.text: Shortened shadow I'm not sure in range

indicators.note: shortened tells us to cut the final letter off the ghostly word

parts.note: a spectre is a ghost or shadowy apparition
um is the noise of hesitation when unsure

explanation.surface: A hesitant speaker describes a shadow that fell short across a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortened' trims the last E from SPECTRE, leaving SPECTR.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full range or scale, as in the political spectrum from left to right.

clue.text: Trick all done the wrong way, as often failing

indicators.note: the wrong way means the phrase for finished is written backwards

parts.note: all up means finished or done for

indicators.note: failing means the letters go wrong, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A trick that was done wrongly fails, as tricks often do.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL UP reversed gives PULLA; 'failing' rearranges AS OFTEN into FAST ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means to deceive or con someone, which is to trick them.

indicators.note: hear tells us to go by how the word is spoken

parts.note: a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

explanation.surface: Listen to the dog howling for such a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a length of time but is a goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian farewell is a casual goodbye, like saying see you.

indicators.note: popping means the drug letter is popped into the gathering word

parts.note: a rally is a mass gathering
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A jolly rally where the crowd pops ecstasy pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' is the British adverb meaning very, as in jolly good.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an intensifier, both words mean very or truly.

parts.note: other means different

explanation.surface: A man describes a relative who is very unlike him.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent is a close family relative.

clue.text: Pasty: every bit eaten by pig

indicators.note: eaten by puts the first piece inside the pig's word, swallowed whole

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
every bit is all of it

explanation.surface: A Cornish pasty is gobbled up entirely by a greedy pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' looks like the Cornish pie but is the adjective for a pale complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an unhealthy, pale, yellowish complexion.

indicators.note: holding means the farmer's word wraps around the following letter

parts.note: a peasant is a small farmer working the land

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A kindly farmer grips one of his animals by the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pleasant is agreeable and amiable, much like a friendly person.

clue.text: Pairing up with hot drunk, is one hammered?

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: Coupling up with a hot partner while drunk: is someone hammered?
explanation.walkthrough: 'hammered' looks like drunk, but the instrument's strings are struck by hammers.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument sounds when felt hammers strike its strings, so it is literally hammered.

definitions.meaning: uncommonly good or excellent, as in a precious collectible
of meat, lightly cooked so it is still red inside

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both exceptionally good and, of steak, barely cooked and pink.

indicators.note: all at sea means confused, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fishing traps are all set out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all at sea' fits the fishing scene but signals the letters of TRAPS are mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A small herring-like sea fish is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Reportedly, tortoises and snails like this fruit

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, pointing to a word that sounds the same

parts.note: tortoises and snails are notoriously slow movers

explanation.surface: Gossip says tortoises and snails enjoy eating this fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like this' seems to mean 'enjoy', but describes how tortoises and snails move.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sour blackthorn berry is a fruit, used to flavour gin.

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub, or bar
Mudd is the setter, so Mudd's is the setter's own: my

explanation.surface: The setter declares a drunkard crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang word means crazy, just as bonkers does.

clue.text: Ships going at a rate of knots?

definitions.text: going at a rate of knots?
definitions.meaning: moving fast; the question mark nods to knots as a ship's speed

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a navy's ships and also means swift, as in fleet of foot.

clue.text: Meek revolutionary in City Hall bullied, along with similar types?

indicators.note: in places the turned word within the jumbled letters
bullied means knocked about, so the letters of the two words are shuffled
revolutionary means turned around, so the meek word is read backwards

parts.note: tame means docile or meek

explanation.surface: A meek rebel is bullied in City Hall alongside others of the same type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meek revolutionary' reads as a timid rebel, but 'revolutionary' simply turns the meek word round; the scrambled City Hall letters split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Grouping things thematically means placing them by topic, together with similar types.

parts.note: a strike is a walkout by workers
up means over, as in time is up

explanation.surface: The strike is over, so the band can begin again.
explanation.definitionFit: A band strikes up a tune when it begins to play music.

clue.text: Light bite he fed to small fish

indicators.note: fed to means the bite and he go inside the fish word

parts.note: fry are young fish
to bite is to eat

explanation.surface: A man feeds a light snack to tiny fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soft and weightless like a feather is light, as in a light sponge.

clue.text: Place of combat where a politician punched, intensity of feeling concerning

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
to punch someone is to hit them
heat is intensity of emotion, as in the heat of the moment
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A politician gets punched in a heated row at the place where fights happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiators fought in Roman arenas, so an oval open-air arena is a place of combat.

definitions.meaning: British slang for a police officer
a low-value British coin, the question mark marking it as an example

explanation.definitionFit: Copper is slang for a police officer, and a penny is a bronze coin called a copper.

clue.text: What's so funny? Is it combat trousers?

indicators.note: trousers as a verb means pockets, so the answer is pocketed in the words

explanation.surface: Someone laughing asks whether combat trousers are a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like the garment, but as a verb it means to pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is a funny television show, so it answers the question.

indicators.note: after reflection means the party word is mirrored, so read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: Having thought it over, a party celebrates God being elected.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief god of Norse mythology is an example of a god.

indicators.note: back tells us the word for breaks is read in reverse

parts.note: to knap is to break or chip stones such as flint

explanation.surface: A slap on the back that breaks something.
explanation.walkthrough: KNAP is an old word for chipping flint into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a slap, especially on the bottom, which is what a spank is.

definitions.meaning: a pale fresh green named after the herb
to coin is to make money by stamping metal

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a pale green and, as a verb, means striking coins at the Royal Mint.

clue.text: Relations, first of all, can leave at noon

indicators.note: first of all takes the opening letter of every word that follows

explanation.surface: Family members, first of all, are allowed to leave at noon.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a group of families sharing descent, so its members are relations.

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pops means nips, as in nipping out to the shop

explanation.surface: A dancer's pirouette suddenly pops up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a rapid turn on one foot, which is a spin.

definitions.meaning: belonging to one particular person or thing, as in a custom unique to a region

explanation.definitionFit: The word means odd, and also distinctive to a single person or place.

indicators.note: stuffing means the dish goes inside, packed into the other word

parts.note: ace means excellent or terrific
a pie is a baked dish; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Every serving of the dish has a terrific stuffing.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means for each one, as in costing a pound per item.

clue.text: Fruit collected by staff for Bacchus, say?

indicators.note: collected by means the fruit is gathered inside the staff word

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
a mango is a tropical fruit

explanation.surface: Fruit is gathered on a staff for the wine god's feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus was the Roman deity of wine, so he is one example, hence 'say'.

definitions.meaning: brisk and fast, as in a lively pace
stylish, as in a well-dressed person

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fast and brief, and neat and fashionable, as in a stylish dresser.
